highlights.content: * [Login](https://www.thelec.net/member/login.html) * [Join](https://www.thelec.net/member/index.html) * [Mobile](https://www.thelec.net/member/index.html) * UPDATE : 2026-11-10 08:53 (Tues) * [KOREAN](http://www.thelec.kr/) [![The Elec Inc.](https://cdn.thelec.net/image/logo/toplogo_20260408103815.png)](https://www.thelec.net) [![The Elec Inc.](https://cdn.thelec.net/image/logo/printlogo_20260408103815.png)](https://www.thelec.net) Rebellions, Nvidia to Build Sovereign AI Infrastructure in Korea Character Size Settings 가 The body content of the article will be changed to this letter size. 스크롤 이동 상태바 # Rebellions, Nvidia to Build Sovereign AI Infrastructure in Korea ## R200-based AI inference rack to be developed and tested at SK Telecom data centers * JEONG IL JOO * Published 2026.11.10 08:51 * Reply 0 Character Size Settings 가 가 The body content of the article will be changed to this letter size. 이 기사를 공유합니다 ![](https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/202611/15444_15767_659.jpg) Rebellions is partnering with Nvidia and SK Telecom (SKT) to build a Korean-standard sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure based on next-generation neural processing units (NPUs). The project will connect Rebellions’ NPUs with Nvidia’s open infrastructure platform through NVLink Fusion, with the resulting systems to be deployed and tested at SKT’s AI data centers. Rebellions CEO Park Sung-hyun unveiled the plan at Nvidia AI Day Seoul 2026 on Nov. 9. The three companies signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) the same day. Rebellions will develop a rack-scale AI inference system using its next-generation R200 NPU and Nvidia’s MGX server rack architecture. The R200 succeeds the R100 NPU, which is equipped with fifth-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM3E). The system will use NVLink Fusion interconnect technology to enable a scale-up architecture connecting the NPU with AI computing platforms, including central processing units (CPUs) and graphics processing units (GPUs), within a server rack. The R200 is being designed for low-latency, high-efficiency inference of frontier AI models, including mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. Rebellions aims to begin supplying R200 systems in 2028. By leveraging Nvidia’s MGX ecosystem, the company plans to shorten rack system development timelines and reduce deployment risks. SKT will deploy the system in its AI data centers for testing under real-world operating conditions. The system will use a distributed inference approach that assigns different stages of AI inference to the most suitable chips, including GPUs and NPUs. This is expected to reduce power consumption and total cost of ownership (TCO) for large-scale AI services. The three companies aim to establish a “Sovereign AI Token Factory,” a sovereign AI data center infrastructure designed to generate tokens at scale. They plan to introduce standards applicable across public institutions and the private sector and accelerate market adoption. Rebellions intends to build a track record through deployments at SKT’s AI data centers and public-facing services before expanding its presence in overseas markets. ![JEONG IL JOO의 프로필 이미지](https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/member/1week_20250825010403.jpg) [JEONG IL JOO](https://www.thelec.net/news/articleList.html?sc_area=I&sc_word=1week&view_type=sm) [1week@thelec.kr](mailto:1week@thelec.kr) [View other news](https://www.thelec.net/news/articleList.html?sc_area=I&sc_word=1week&view_type=sm) Copyright © The Elec Inc. highlights.content: # Rebellions R200 NPU Racks Get NVLink Fusion, With NVIDIA GPUs on Prefill and NPUs on Decode, Deploying in 2028 NVIDIA, Rebellions, and SK Telecom announced a plan to build sovereign AI inference infrastructure in South Korea around Rebellions’ next-generation R200 neural processing unit, connected inside the rack with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion and built on the NVIDIA MGX rack architecture. SK Telecom will deploy the systems in its AI data center alongside its models and services. The three companies expect R200 systems to be ready for deployment in 2028. ## NVLink Fusion Connects R200 NPUs Rebellions is designing the R200 for low-latency, energy-efficient inference on frontier models, including multitrillion-parameter mixture-of-experts models. [NVLink Fusion](https://www.storagereview.com/news/the-network-is-the-accelerator-inside-the-technologies-powering-ai-factories) is NVIDIA’s program for bringing custom silicon onto its scale-up fabric: a chipmaker integrates NVLink into its processor and gains access to NVIDIA’s NVLink switching, its high-bandwidth, low-latency networking, and the surrounding infrastructure ecosystem. Rebellions plans to use it to link R200 NPUs within a rack over NVLink scale-up networking and to tie those processors into the NVIDIA platform as part of a rack-scale system. The companies have not disclosed R200 specifications, the NVLink bandwidth per NPU, or any performance results for the planned configuration. Rebellions lists the Rebel100 as its current silicon, and the R200 announcement says nothing about memory, process node, or power, so the step between the two generations is unknown. ## MGX Rack Architecture Supports System Development NVIDIA’s [MGX rack architecture](https://www.storagereview.com/news/msi-ocp-2026-liquid-cooled-cg681-s6093-mgx-rack-32-rtx-pro-6000) and reference designs give Rebellions a starting point for the system, along with access to the original design manufacturers and component suppliers already building MGX hardware. MGX defines the shared pieces of a rack, including footprint, power delivery, and cooling, so GPU systems and NPU systems can occupy the same data center design. SK Telecom plans to deploy the R200 systems in its AI data center on the standardized MGX rack, which lets it plan power and cooling before the processor is final. ## GPUs for Prefill, NPUs for Decode The most interesting technical detail is the inference split the three companies plan to develop. Inference has two phases with different hardware demands: prefill, which processes the prompt and is typically compute-bound, and decode, which generates tokens one at a time and is typically bound by memory bandwidth and latency. The proposed configuration runs prefill on NVIDIA GPUs and decode on Rebellions NPUs, with the two connected over the NVLink fabric. The stated goals are higher inference throughput and better power efficiency. The benefit of handing decode to an NPU remains a design intent until systems exist, but the logic makes sense on paper. Disaggregated prefill and decode is already common practice across GPU pools, including in NVIDIA’s Dynamo serving framework; splitting the two phases across different processor architectures over NVLink is the new part. Rebellions cofounder and CEO Sunghyun Park said the collaboration combines the company’s AI silicon and system design with NVIDIA’s interconnect and rack-scale capabilities and SK Telecom’s models and data center operations, with the aim of low-latency, energy-efficient inference for frontier models at scale. ## SK Telecom Connects Models and Services SK Telecom brings the models and the customers. It plans to run its proprietary foundation models, including A.X K2, on the infrastructure, along with public-facing services developed through the Korean government’s AI for All project. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English ![Anthropic releases Fable 5.2 with lower pricing and higher coding scores](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Fanthropic-releases-fable-52-with-lower-pricing-and-higher-coding-scores_gen_1794254703304-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #Business # Anthropic releases Fable 5.2 with lower pricing and higher coding scores • ![Tomáš Novák](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Ftomas-novak.webp&w=64&q=75) [Tomáš Novák](/author/tomas-novak) •2 min read Share this article Anthropic launched Fable 5.2 with a price cut and stronger coding benchmark results, sharpening its pitch to developers and enterprise teams. The move raises pressure in a crowded market for AI coding tools. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com) released Fable 5.2 with a lower price and stronger coding scores, pairing performance gains with a cost reduction aimed at developers and businesses that build software with AI. ## Business news Anthropic positioned Fable 5.2 as an upgrade for coding work while reducing the price customers pay to use it. The company tied the release to improved results on coding evaluations, a signal that it wants buyers to compare the model on both output quality and cost. For software teams, those two variables shape adoption. Engineering leaders weigh model accuracy, reliability on code tasks, and the bill that follows heavy use in editors, code review, testing, and internal automation. A release that improves scores and lowers price targets both sides of that decision. ## Market context The market for AI coding models has become a contest over performance, latency, and unit economics. Anthropic competes with [OpenAI](https://openai.com), Google, and a growing set of model providers that sell coding capabilities through APIs, chat products, and developer tools. Buyers can switch providers or route tasks across models, which keeps pricing and benchmark claims under scrutiny. Coding remains one of the clearest commercial uses for large language models because companies can measure time saved, defect rates, and developer throughput. That measurability pushes vendors to publish benchmark results and adjust pricing to win volume. A price cut can expand usage among startups and individual developers, while stronger coding scores can support larger contracts with enterprise engineering organizations. ## What it means Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 release reflects a familiar strategy in infrastructure markets: improve the product and lower the barrier to adoption at the same time. If the coding gains hold up in production workflows, lower pricing can drive more API calls and deeper integration into developer pipelines. That tradeoff can reduce revenue per request while increasing total demand. The release also raises the competitive stakes for rivals selling coding-focused models. Competitors face a choice: match the price, defend higher prices with clear performance advantages, or bundle coding features into broader platforms. For customers, the shift creates room to renegotiate contracts, test alternatives, and set stricter requirements for benchmark transparency and real-world code quality. highlights.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [![](https://www.engineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Engineering.com_color-TM-scaled.png)](https://www.engineering.com) [Subscribe](https://www.engineering.com/subscribe/) [Industry News](https://www.engineering.com/category/industry/industry-news/) # NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom advance Korea’s sovereign AI The collaboration will integrate Korean-designed R200 processors with NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion and MGX rack architecture for AI deployment. NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a collaboration to advance Korea’s sovereign AI infrastructure — using NVIDIA NVLink Fusion to bring together NVIDIA’s open infrastructure platform, Rebellions’ Korean-designed AI processors and SK Telecom’s AI data center, model and service capabilities. As part of the agreement, Rebellions will use NVLink Fusion to connect its Rebel R200 neural processing units (NPUs) to the NVIDIA platform, and harness the NVIDIA MGX rack architecture for rack-scale system development. SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems, drawing on its AI data center operations expertise, proprietary models and services. Supported by Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), the collaboration aims to support AI services tailored to Korea’s language, industries and priorities, connecting Korean semiconductor development with the systems and operational capabilities needed to deliver AI at scale. ### **Scaling silicon innovation with NVIDIA’s open infrastructure platform** NVLink Fusion extends NVIDIA’s vertically integrated, horizontally open AI platform to custom XPUs. It enables chipmakers to combine specialized silicon with NVIDIA’s high-bandwidth, low-latency scale-up networking and established infrastructure ecosystem, helping improve performance, reduce deployment risk and accelerate time to market. Rebellions is developing its next-generation R200 NPU, optimized for low-latency and energy-efficient inference using frontier models, including multitrillion-parameter [mixture-of-experts](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/mixture-of-experts/) models. Through NVLink Fusion, Rebellions will connect its R200 NPUs within a rack through [NVIDIA NVLink](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/nvlink/) scale-up networking. The NVIDIA MGX rack architecture and reference designs will support development of the systems, while the MGX ecosystem gives Rebellions access to an established supply chain of original design manufacturers and component suppliers. ### **Connecting infrastructure, models and services** SK Telecom brings experience building and operating AI data centers, alongside its proprietary foundation models and public-facing AI services. Building on its [long-standing collaboration with NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/sk-telecom-ai-infrastructure) in AI development and sovereign infrastructure, SK Telecom plans to connect these capabilities and deploy them in its AI data center using the standardized MGX rack architecture to deliver full-stack sovereign AI. The MGX rack architecture provides a foundation for GPU and NPU systems to share data center design elements, including rack footprint, power delivery and cooling. This approach can support infrastructure planning alongside Rebellions’ processor and system development. The companies plan to develop an approach to disaggregated inference, assigning different stages of AI response generation to the processor architecture best suited to each task. Their planned work includes using NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput and power efficiency. SK Telecom plans to connect this infrastructure with its proprietary foundation models and public-facing services, including those under the government’s AI for All project, to advance its full-stack sovereign AI strategy. ### **Supporting sovereign AI infrastructure with NVLink Fusion** MSIT is supporting collaboration between NVIDIA and Korean NPU companies, beginning...

highlights.content: # A benchmark called 'LLM AssBench' has emerged that uses AI to create '3DCG buttocks' and compares their performance. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/00_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/00.png) A benchmark called 'LLM AssBench' has been released that compares the performance of AI by having it create 3D CG models of human buttocks. The AI-generated buttocks can be rotated and clicked to make them jiggle in the browser, and various AI-generated buttocks can be lined up and compared. **LLM AssBench** <https://assbench.com/> **AssBench is all You need to benchmark LLM Harness Intelligence /s <https://grigio.org/assbench-is-all-you-need-to-benchmark-llm-harness-intelligence-s/>** **[The Smartest benchmark to feel LLM 'intelligence'. ASSBENCH - YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2BfygMivxIQ)** When comparing the performance of AI, benchmarks that involve solving mathematical problems or writing programs are often used. However, there is a challenge in accurately measuring an AI's ability to solve problems, as widely known problems may be included in the AI's training data. That's when developer Luigi released LLM AssBench in September 2026. LLM AssBench is a benchmark that examines how well AI can understand and incorporate three-dimensional shapes and complex conditions into its programs by giving the same instructions to multiple AIs and comparing the resulting 3DCG. The subject chosen for this benchmark was the human buttocks. The instructions for the AI were to 'create a realistic and interactive 3D model of a human buttock in a single HTML file.' The JavaScript library 'Three.js' was used for 3DCG rendering, and it was necessary to represent the human body from the waist to the thighs and reproduce even the texture of the skin without using external images or 3D models. Furthermore, the AI needs to be able to rotate the buttocks with drag gestures and make them sway softly when clicked. In other words, the AI needs to be programmed to take into account not only the shape of the human body but also its physical movements. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/snap9869_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/snap9869.png) The LLM AssBench website features buttocks generated by various AIs, including Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT, and Google's Gemini. This emerging architecture introduces new complexities and requires significant adaptation in established software development fields. * [TechGig](/agency/87450652/TechGig "TechGig") * Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 05:00 AM IST ## Highlights * Agentic AI architecture integrates AI agent systems into microservices and cloud-native setups. * New security risks include prompt injection and instruction confusion for AI agents. * Context engineering manages LLM context for optimal outcomes and reduced hallucinations. * Observability is critical for non-deterministic agentic AI systems, requiring detailed logging. [Agentic AI](/tag/agentic+ai) architecture extends [microservices](/tag/microservices) and [cloud-native](/tag/cloud-native) architectures with AI agent systems, according to InfoQ. This new architecture adds a significant degree of complexity, necessitating that architects and engineers learn new concepts, techniques, and technologies. Many well-established areas within predominant [software architecture](/tag/software+architecture) types require rethinking or substantial adaptation to meet the unique requirements of agentic AI systems. ### Emergence of Agentic AI Systems Agentic AI systems have evolved from simple single-agent solutions to multi-agent systems (MAS) where multiple agents collaborate in various topologies. Context engineering focuses on ensuring that the context used maximises the LLM's likelihood of producing the desired outcome and minimises hallucinations. Integrating agentic AI significantly alters the security model, introducing threats like prompt injection, instruction confusion, and tool output poisoning. Existing access-control models are ill-suited for AI agents, prompting proposals for new permission models like capability-scoped permissions and task-scoped credentials. [Observability](/tag/observability) is crucial for non-deterministic agentic AI systems, requiring comprehensive coverage across logging, metrics, tracing, and alerting. Without behavioral visibility, an agent with valid credentials could act across your environment at machine speed and nothing would flag it as unusual. [By Russell Smith on Nov 09, 2026](https://petri.com/author/russell-smith/ "View all articles by Russell Smith") ![copilot studio agents hero approved](https://petri.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/copilot-studio-agents-hero-approved.png) AI agent security is creating a familiar problem for IT teams. Enterprises are giving autonomous agents access to applications, infrastructure, and sensitive data, sometimes with the same excessive privileges organizations have spent decades trying to eliminate from human accounts. The difference is speed. An overprivileged human identity presents a security risk and an overprivileged AI agent can potentially act across an environment at machine speed. *“These are identities, these are entities,”* said Heath Mullins, Chief Evangelist at [ExtraHop](https://www.extrahop.com/) and a former [Forrester](https://www.forrester.com/) analyst. *“They should be assigned appropriate permissions to accomplish the task at hand. And that task should not be overly broad.”* But least privilege only answers one part of the AI security problem. Organizations also need to know whether agents behave as expected after they receive access. ## AI agent security starts with least privilege The [principle of least privilege](https://identitymanagementinstitute.org/the-principle-of-least-privilege/) isn’t new. Organizations have spent years trying to stop administrators, applications, and service accounts from receiving unnecessary permissions. Mullins argues that enterprises should apply the same thinking to AI agents. Some organizations, he said, are giving agents broad administrative permissions to find vulnerabilities, recommend remediation, and identify systems requiring patches. That sounds attractive because an agent can automate work across an enterprise. But it can also create an autonomous administrator. *“Don’t let it go carte blanche,”* Mullins said. *“This is your task and that’s it.”* [Microsoft Copilot](https://petri.com/what-is-microsoft-copilot-studio/), Gemini, Claude, and other AI systems need access to information to provide useful results. Organizations therefore need controls defining what an agent can access and what actions it can perform. ## AI makes excessive permissions more dangerous AI doesn’t necessarily reinvent the basic stages of a cyberattack. Attackers still need an entry point and may escalate privileges, establish command and control, and move laterally. What changes is the speed. *“The attack cycle hasn’t really changed that much,”* Mullins said. *“The execution speed is what has changed.”* An AI-driven attack can potentially discover vulnerabilities, escalate privileges, and move through the network faster than a human attacker. *“We’re not talking weeks, days, even hours anymore. We’re talking minutes, and a human simply cannot keep up with that anymore,”* Mullins said. That makes excessive permissions particularly dangerous. But restricting permissions isn’t enough, because authorization tells security teams what an identity is permitted to do rather than whether its behavior is normal. ## Permissions don’t tell you what an AI agent actually does An AI agent might have legitimate credentials and authorization to access several enterprise systems. Some organizations, he said, are giving agents broad administrative permissions to find vulnerabilities, recommend remediation, and identify systems requiring patches. Attackers still need an entry point and may escalate privileges, establish command and control, and move laterally. What changes is the speed. *“The attack cycle hasn’t really changed that much,”* Mullins said. *“The execution speed is what has changed.”* An AI-driven attack can potentially discover vulnerabilities, escalate privileges, and move through the network faster than a human attacker. *“We’re not talking weeks, days, even hours anymore. But new AI models are leading to robotic innovations that give him "goosebumps."* By [Jason Pohl](https://news.berkeley.edu/author/jpohl/) ![A large, blue robotic arm holds a small part over a series of buckets and containers.](https://news.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Ambi-Robotics-AmbiKit_2.jpg) The new discipline of "agentic robotics" could revolutionize robotics, said Ken Goldberg, a UC Berkeley roboticist. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.” Courtesy of Ambi Robotics November 9, 2026 In recent months, [artificial intelligence agents](https://news.berkeley.edu/2026/08/19/uc-berkeley-computer-scientist-on-the-promise-and-perils-of-agentic-ai/) that can reason, plan and use external tools to accomplish multistep tasks have already reshaped [computer coding](https://www.businessinsider.com/ai-coding-changing-software-developer-role-2026-3?utm_source=chatgpt.com), [online shopping,](https://www.wsj.com/business/ai-agents-bring-new-headaches-to-online-sellers-d2dc84b4) [dinner reservations](https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/tech-news/trying-get-restaurant-reservation-get-ready-compete-ai-agents-rcna599738) and [cyberattacks](https://www.reuters.com/legal/government/how-one-hacker-used-ai-agents-few-thousand-dollars-break-into-scores-sites-2026-10-19/). Robotics might be next. [Ken Goldberg](https://www2.eecs.berkeley.edu/Faculty/Homepages/goldberg.html), a UC Berkeley roboticist and professor of engineering, said new models make it possible for teams of AI agents to develop robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments and revise the code when something doesn’t work. Goldberg, with Spencer Huang, director of robotics engineering at NVIDIA, and a team of researchers call the new approach “agentic robotics.” They said it could offer a way around two obstacles in the field: the enormous amounts of data needed to train robots and the intense engineering efforts required to program them, both of which can demand vast amounts of physical and technical resources to accomplish. ![Ken Goldberg profile photo, with his head resting on his hand](https://news.berkeley.edu/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/Ken-Goldberg-0-600dpi-photo-by-Chris-Michel-683x1024.jpeg) Ken Goldberg “Agentic robotics is a fundamental shift in how robots are controlled,” Goldberg said. “Instead of collecting massive amounts of data and hand-tuning every behavior, teams of agents can quickly generate, test and refine robot programs that allow human engineers to interpret how the programs work for fine-tuning and verification.” Goldberg, who was recently [inducted into the National Academy of Engineering](https://news.berkeley.edu/2026/02/11/four-uc-berkeley-faculty-elected-to-national-academy-of-engineering/), is presenting the new approach and results from months of testing this week at the [Conference on Robot Learning](https://www.corl.org/). The agent reportedly escaped its controlled testing environment and exploited four security weaknesses, accessing business records and customer communications over five days. LLMs.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [News](/) English ![Anthropic releases Fable 5.2 with lower pricing and higher coding scores](/_next/image?url=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.lavx.hu%2Fapi%2Fmedia%2Ffile%2Fanthropic-releases-fable-52-with-lower-pricing-and-higher-coding-scores_gen_1794254703304-1200x630.jpg&w=3840&q=75) #Business # Anthropic releases Fable 5.2 with lower pricing and higher coding scores • ![Tomáš Novák](/_next/image?url=%2Fauthors%2Ftomas-novak.webp&w=64&q=75) [Tomáš Novák](/author/tomas-novak) •2 min read Share this article Anthropic launched Fable 5.2 with a price cut and stronger coding benchmark results, sharpening its pitch to developers and enterprise teams. The move raises pressure in a crowded market for AI coding tools. [Anthropic](https://www.anthropic.com) released Fable 5.2 with a lower price and stronger coding scores, pairing performance gains with a cost reduction aimed at developers and businesses that build software with AI. ## Business news Anthropic positioned Fable 5.2 as an upgrade for coding work while reducing the price customers pay to use it. The company tied the release to improved results on coding evaluations, a signal that it wants buyers to compare the model on both output quality and cost. For software teams, those two variables shape adoption. Engineering leaders weigh model accuracy, reliability on code tasks, and the bill that follows heavy use in editors, code review, testing, and internal automation. A release that improves scores and lowers price targets both sides of that decision. ## Market context The market for AI coding models has become a contest over performance, latency, and unit economics. Anthropic competes with [OpenAI](https://openai.com), Google, and a growing set of model providers that sell coding capabilities through APIs, chat products, and developer tools. Buyers can switch providers or route tasks across models, which keeps pricing and benchmark claims under scrutiny. Coding remains one of the clearest commercial uses for large language models because companies can measure time saved, defect rates, and developer throughput. That measurability pushes vendors to publish benchmark results and adjust pricing to win volume. A price cut can expand usage among startups and individual developers, while stronger coding scores can support larger contracts with enterprise engineering organizations. ## What it means Anthropic’s Fable 5.2 release reflects a familiar strategy in infrastructure markets: improve the product and lower the barrier to adoption at the same time. If the coding gains hold up in production workflows, lower pricing can drive more API calls and deeper integration into developer pipelines. That tradeoff can reduce revenue per request while increasing total demand. The release also raises the competitive stakes for rivals selling coding-focused models. Competitors face a choice: match the price, defend higher prices with clear performance advantages, or bundle coding features into broader platforms. For customers, the shift creates room to renegotiate contracts, test alternatives, and set stricter requirements for benchmark transparency and real-world code quality. LLMs.content: # A benchmark called 'LLM AssBench' has emerged that uses AI to create '3DCG buttocks' and compares their performance. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/00_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/00.png) A benchmark called 'LLM AssBench' has been released that compares the performance of AI by having it create 3D CG models of human buttocks. The AI-generated buttocks can be rotated and clicked to make them jiggle in the browser, and various AI-generated buttocks can be lined up and compared. **LLM AssBench** <https://assbench.com/> **AssBench is all You need to benchmark LLM Harness Intelligence /s <https://grigio.org/assbench-is-all-you-need-to-benchmark-llm-harness-intelligence-s/>** **[The Smartest benchmark to feel LLM 'intelligence'. ASSBENCH - YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2BfygMivxIQ)** When comparing the performance of AI, benchmarks that involve solving mathematical problems or writing programs are often used. However, there is a challenge in accurately measuring an AI's ability to solve problems, as widely known problems may be included in the AI's training data. That's when developer Luigi released LLM AssBench in September 2026. LLM AssBench is a benchmark that examines how well AI can understand and incorporate three-dimensional shapes and complex conditions into its programs by giving the same instructions to multiple AIs and comparing the resulting 3DCG. The subject chosen for this benchmark was the human buttocks. The instructions for the AI were to 'create a realistic and interactive 3D model of a human buttock in a single HTML file.' The JavaScript library 'Three.js' was used for 3DCG rendering, and it was necessary to represent the human body from the waist to the thighs and reproduce even the texture of the skin without using external images or 3D models. Furthermore, the AI needs to be able to rotate the buttocks with drag gestures and make them sway softly when clicked. In other words, the AI needs to be programmed to take into account not only the shape of the human body but also its physical movements. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/snap9869_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/snap9869.png) The LLM AssBench website features buttocks generated by various AIs, including Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT, and Google's Gemini. You can compare up to four results side-by-side, and also check the type of AI used and the test settings. As of the time of writing, 42 generated results, including past versions, are registered. [![](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/snap9870_m.png)](https://i.gzn.jp/img/2026/11/09/llm-assbench/snap9870.png) Luigi pointed out that even small-scale AIs can sometimes generate 3DCG of a quality close to that of large-scale AIs, and stated that when judging the performance of an AI, it is important not only to consider the size of the model, but also how accurately it can perform tasks that are suited to the purpose. LLM AssBench is also planning a system to evaluate the realism, usability, physical movement, and operational stability of the generated results on a total of 40 points. Luigi says that through the evaluation results, they want to make it easier to select an AI that can produce sufficiently high-quality results while keeping costs down. LLMs.content: # Meituan releases the open weights of its LongCat-2.5 LLM with vision under a permissive MIT License Meituan released the weights for LongCat-2.5 on Nov. 9, one week after introducing the model. The Chinese food delivery and e-commerce company published the checkpoint on Hugging Face under the MIT License, giving developers another way to run a model that can inspect screenshots and video, work through a codebase, and write or revise software over multiple steps. The strongest case for testing LongCat-2.5 is a job that requires both visual judgment and coding. Think of a developer handing an agent a screenshot of a broken checkout flow, asking it to find the relevant components in a repository, and having it propose a patch and check the result in a browser. Meituan’s hosted API pricing makes that experiment relatively inexpensive. The more useful question for buyers is whether it can handle enough visual and coding work at its discounted API rates to reserve premium models for harder jobs. Operating the full model inside a private network presents a different calculation. One important note for U.S. and Western enterprises considering this model: Chinese AI models are facing growing scrutiny in Washington. In October, the U.S. Department of Homeland Security disclosed an order directing federal civilian agencies to exclude DeepSeek from procurement and remove its technology from covered systems, including implementations supplied by third parties. The order targets DeepSeek and its affiliates. VentureBeat found no publicly disclosed U.S. federal procurement or use restriction that specifically names Meituan or LongCat-2.5 as of Nov. 9. But the rules can change quickly. As VentureBeat reported in February, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced on Feb. 27 that he was directing the Pentagon to designate Anthropic a “Supply-Chain Risk to National Security.” He formalized the designation on March 3. The two cases show how quickly a dispute or a supply-chain decision can change what agencies and their suppliers can use ## Where visual understanding earns its keep In its technical write-up, Meituan describes a model that represents visual information as tokens and processes it alongside text. Its API guide shows how developers can submit screenshots, charts, images, and videos. Images can be embedded in a request or supplied by URL. The documented video interface takes a URL, a meaningful constraint for teams working with internal screen recordings. For frontend and product engineering, a good initial task is a visual regression with a known fix. Give the agent the failing screenshot, access to a test repository, and a way to render the patched page. Check whether it finds the cause, makes a targeted change, and preserves keyboard navigation and responsive behavior. A similar workflow can turn design references into prototypes, but the test should check whether the output follows the team’s component library and interaction rules as well as whether it looks right. Meituan highlighted developer demos that included a car-launch site from Tasihi, a fantasy game interface from AI Maverick Frank, and a shop management site from Aigc Lancet. The company’s own examples include an interactive fluid simulation and a 3D exhibition. These are good leads for teams building demos or internal tools. A storefront prototype and a production storefront have different acceptance criteria. For the latter, the generated code still has to pass the same functional, accessibility, and maintenance checks as a human-authored change. ## LongCat gains on its predecessor while newer rivals set a higher bar The clearest comparison in Meituan’s evaluation is with its predecessor. LongCat-2.5 scores 88.4 versus 70.8 on Terminal Bench v2.1, 64.6 versus 9.7 on DeepSWE v1.1, and 58.3 versus 33.1 on the SWE Atlas codebase question-answering test. By pruning up to 37% of the model's expert modules, Nota reduced memory usage while retaining more than 99% of the original model's performance on a scientific reasoning benchmark. The freed-up memory was reinvested to support context windows of up to 1 million tokens and to enable speculative decoding for faster response generation. According to the company's own estimates, initial GPU purchase costs fall by up to 20% and cloud rental fees by up to 22%. The result lowers the barrier to deploying large models for companies with limited infrastructure budgets, even as it may temper demand at the high end of the GPU market. ##### Key Elements ![South Korea's Nota Runs 2.8-Trillion-Parameter AI Without Nvidia B300, Cutting GPU Costs by 20%](https://img.biggo.com/JzXdrI_sL6XUZ4aKgKhF6RzcrCKPFjJJo-mcQqxUFi4/fit/1720/0/sm/0/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbWcuYmdvLm9uZS9uZXdzLWltYWdlL2FpX2dlbmVyYXRlZC8yMDI2LTExLzQ0ZTgyMjNiLWFkM2QtNDY4NS1hZmE1LTE4Y2MxODAzYTFkNF8xNzk0Mjc2MjQ4X2RlZmF1bHQuanBn.webp) Nota, a South Korean AI model optimization company, has succeeded in running a massive large language model (LLM) with 2.8 trillion parameters without the latest high-performance GPUs. By getting the model to run on the previous-generation Nvidia B200 instead of the newest B300, the company expects to cut enterprises' upfront AI infrastructure investment by as much as 20%. Nota said on the 10th that it had optimized Kimi K3.1 Pro, an open-weight model from China's Moonshot AI, allowing a model that previously required eight B300 GPUs to run on a setup of eight B200 GPUs. Kimi K3.1 Pro ranks among the largest open-weight models publicly available by parameter count. The larger the model, the more GPU memory and compute resources it needs to run, driving up the cost of building and operating corporate infrastructure. The key to the optimization is a pruning technique that selectively removes expert modules responsible for specific tasks within the model. Nota said it cut the number of expert modules by up to 37% while retaining more than 99% of the original model's score on GPQA Diamond, a benchmark that evaluates advanced scientific reasoning. The memory freed up by the slimming was reinvested in expanding the amount of information the model can process at once. On a setup of eight B200 GPUs, the model with 30% of its expert modules removed handles context windows of up to 512,000 tokens, while the version with 37% removed handles up to 1 million tokens. Nota also boosted response generation speed by supporting "speculative decoding," a technique in which a smaller auxiliary model proposes the next answer and the main model verifies it in a single pass. The cost benefits are also confirmed in Nota's own price comparison. Running the same model on B200 instead of B300 cuts initial GPU purchase costs by up to about 20%. Image Credit: Jack\_the\_sparow / Shutterstock* In a recent study published in the journal **[*Scientific Reports*](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-026-78926-z)**, researchers at the University of the Pacific School of Pharmacy, Stockton, USA, compared the accuracy of five large language models (LLMs) in answering infectious disease-related pharmacy examination questions across different pharmacy subject areas, cognitive levels, and question formats. ## Background Can artificial intelligence (AI) reliably answer questions that future healthcare professionals must master? LLMs have the potential to be educational tools that generate explanations and answers to support interactive learning. Their use in healthcare may also raise ethical concerns. Incorrect information may affect students' and educators' understanding of clinical concepts and potentially influence clinical judgment. Previous studies evaluating LLMs in the discipline of pharmacy education showed inconsistent performance. LLMs may raise concerns about academic integrity and the development of critical thinking skills. Further research is needed to establish their reliability across pharmacy subjects and cognitive levels. ## About the study The researchers conducted a comparative analysis of five commercially available LLMs using examination questions from an Integrated Clinical Sciences Infectious Diseases course, a required second-year course in the accelerated three-year Doctor of Pharmacy program at the University of the Pacific School of Pharmacy. The course ran from January to April 2025, and data were collected from May to July 2025. The evaluated models were ChatGPT-4.1 and ChatGPT-4o-mini (OpenAI), Claude Sonnet 4 (Anthropic), Copilot Web/Mobile/Edge (Microsoft), and Gemini 2.5 Flash (Google). The researchers evaluated 227 examination questions drawn from the course, covering medicinal chemistry, clinical microbiology, pharmacology, therapeutics, and pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Bloom's taxonomy was used to classify questions into remember/understand, apply/analyze, and evaluate/create categories. The questions were also categorized by format (multiple-choice or fill-in-the-blank) and whether they included images. Each model received identical prompts and instructions to answer the questions and explain why the selected answer was correct and the alternative options were incorrect. Yet only 25% have done so today. IBM is betting on its strengths — mainframe hardware, hybrid computing assets and a legacy of strong governance — to gain a leg up on the rest of the market, according to theCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante. “In our opinion, IBM has found a differentiated path in enterprise AI by productizing workflow-level outcomes across a stack that, while sometimes confusing, customers generally trust,” he said. “Client Zero proof, a workload-first hybrid design, durable platforms reimagined for agents and a pragmatic quantum roadmap create a credible basis for sustained advantage.” This feature is part of SiliconANGLE Media’s exploration of how enterprise AI has moved beyond the race for model supremacy, with major technology players now focused on enabling governed enterprise AI that delivers trust, reliability and predictable business outcomes. (\* Disclosure below.) ### Building toward an enterprise AI operating model IBM already has a substantial book of business around generative AI, with AI-related software sales and consulting engagements totaling more than $12.5 billion as of Q4 2025, up from $9.5 billion the previous quarter. Many of these capabilities were rolled out as part of a steady drumbeat of announcements leading up to IBM Think 2026 in May. The move positions Concert as the intelligent operations layer of IBM’s broader enterprise AI strategy. The IBM Sovereign Core platform announced at Think 2026 is designed to address the final pillar: governance. It helps enterprises build and operate AI-ready sovereign environments by embedding governance, compliance and operational control directly into the underlying infrastructure. June brought more AI-related announcements: IBM joined OpenAI’s Daybreak Cyber Partner Program, which aims to identify AI-driven cybersecurity threats. AI Product.content: # Anthropic releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, pairing new, record-high benchmarks with 20% API cost reduction What's better than a new frontier model? Try two, both of them achieving new high scores on a variety of third-party benchmarks — all with a 20% cost reduction over API for enterprises and developers. That's exactly what Anthropic has done today: less than an hour ago, the fast-growing generative AI startup announced Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, its latest, most powerful frontier language models for general usage and cyber workflows, respectively, and the results across the board are, once again, nothing short of impressive — dare we say, potentially industry-changing. Both models now cost $8 per million uncached input tokens and $40 per million output tokens, down from $10 and $50 for their predecessors in the 5.1 generation, respectively. Claude API model Standard input / output Cache read Cache write, 5 min / 1 hr Fast input / output Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 $10 / $50 $0.25 $12.50 / $20 No listed rate Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 $8 / $40 $0.20 $10 / $16 $16 / $80 Opus 5.5 $4 / $20 $0.20 $5 / $8 $8 / $40 Fable is available right now on paid Claude plans, in Claude Code and through the Claude Platform (model ID ``` claude-fable-5-2 ``` ), AWS, Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure. Mythos uses the same underlying model with different safeguards and is reserved for vetted cybersecurity and life sciences users in Anthropic's Project Glasswing program. The most useful number for enterprise engineering teams is likely $6.72. That was the average cost of a task on Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 test with Fable 5.2 at High effort, according to Anthropic's System Card on the new models. Opus 5.5, which charges half as much for standard uncached input and output, averaged $12.82 at Max for a nearly identical score. The trade can also go the other way. Turning Fable all the way up to Max drove the average cost to $44.70 and brought its score below what it achieved at the cheaper Xhigh setting, according to Anthropic’s system card. That makes Fable an interesting option for jobs that already burn time and money in retries, such as a migration across an unfamiliar codebase or a bug that survives several rounds of diagnosis. Anthropic itself recommends Opus 5.5 for most coding and knowledge work. Fable can take over an entire job or serve as an advisor that a less expensive model consults when it gets stuck. Each setup buys a different amount of Fable’s time. ## How Fable and Mythos compare with rival models Less than two weeks after Google unveiled Gemini 4 Carbon, the search giant’s latest frontier model, Anthropic has put up a set of scores that reshuffles the field. But the two releases look different from the buyer’s side. Google announced Carbon on October 28 and began by giving access to selected cybersecurity defenders through its Fairwind program. Carbon remains in limited release as of November 9. Most developers who want to put a Gemini 4 model to work today can use Gemini 4 Argon. Those two numbers frame the decision every team faces in November 2026: pay a hosted API by the token, or download the weights and run a self-hosted LLM on your own metal. Four open-weight families dominate that choice right now. Open Source AI.content: [English](/english/) [Industry](/english/industry-en/) # NVIDIA Invests in Motif's 2027 AI Model Funding supports Motif 4's development, targeting global top 5 and open-weight release [By Choi A-ri](/english/people/choi-ari/) Published 2026.11.09. 17:59 Updated 2026.11.09. 18:02 ![On February, Lim Jung-hwan, CEO of Motif Technologies, has an interview with our publication in Seocho-gu, Seoul. Photo by Kim Ji-ho](https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/WHFDZZKZV5FY5AKD5XAEOV2XDI.jpg?auth=b5607e0191aecfcdfb094e97db54f784103663b7c347b60f0cd5e41b1671fe9a&width=616) On February, Lim Jung-hwan, CEO of Motif Technologies, has an interview with our publication in Seocho-gu, Seoul. Photo by Kim Ji-ho Domestic artificial intelligence (AI) model developer Motif Technologies has secured investment from NVIDIA. The funds will be allocated to the development of its next-generation AI model, "Motif 4," which aims for public release in the first quarter of 2027. Motif announced on the 9th that it has finalized investment rounds for the development of its next-generation large language model (LLM) and commenced work on the model. NVIDIA is set to participate in this round alongside existing investors. The exact investment amount was not disclosed. NVIDIA is also expected to join the second round of Series C funding for domestic AI company Upstage. Motif 4 is the successor to "Motif 3," announced in August. Motif has set a goal of entering the top 5 in global AI model performance rankings with the new model. It plans to release the model under an "open-weight" approach, disclosing internal numerical values of the trained model for developers to download and utilize. The predecessor, Motif 3, was developed through the Ministry of Science and ICT’s independent AI foundation model project. In August, it scored 47 points on Artificial Analysis’ comprehensive intelligence index, ranking 4th among open-source models at the time. Motif plans to focus on enhancing usability and commercial viability to a level suitable for real-world services in its successor model. Motif CEO Lim Jeong-hwan stated, “With sufficient resources secured for ‘Motif 4,’ we will pour everything into delivering a groundbreaking result that not only excels technologically but also achieves complete usability and commercial viability.” Editor’s Pick [![Samsung Lions End 12-Year Championship Drought](https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/2YYCPCRSZZDAPA3KEBH6JQFOYU.jpg?auth=778e1fd86c715176749fa674e32b0ece8ad78ff235606345cb8ab79c61df3dce&width=400&height=225&focal=243,81)](/english/industry-en/2026/11/09/DBGDPJE4FRATVDBXZKBGNCSX2I/) [Samsung Lions End 12-Year Championship Drought](/english/industry-en/2026/11/09/DBGDPJE4FRATVDBXZKBGNCSX2I/) 2h ago | Soonchan Park [![NVIDIA CEO's Secret Link to Chinese Intelligence](https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/XU3CYRZR2NC3FENCSMJIUPNKSA.gif?auth=ef7b9d5750b928ea5ae5555130b92c138c61dbcafdc874d8404effe5b8d16976&width=400&height=225&smart=true)](/english/world-en/2026/11/09/LKZAWUHN6BBEPEUPOGURXH2OGQ/) [NVIDIA CEO's Secret Link to Chinese Intelligence](/english/world-en/2026/11/09/LKZAWUHN6BBEPEUPOGURXH2OGQ/) 3h ago | You Jin-woo (ChosunBiz) [![KOSPI Surrenders Gains, Closes Down 0.81%](https://www.chosun.com/resizer/v2/7I5PB4AS7BLKVH5MLON4NR4GCA.jpg?auth=aa7dcefa31b60dd45e2f3d21d19facea2f4c529065516072c79015ff66c1e331&width=400&height=225&focal=866,405)](/english/market-money-en/2026/11/09/FBJVAH2EWVC6HACY77PUUMB7SA/) [KOSPI Surrenders Gains, Closes Down 0.81%](/english/market-money-en/2026/11/09/FBJVAH2EWVC6HACY77PUUMB7SA/) 2h ago | Chae Je-u

Open Source AI.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) Monday, November 9, 2026 [>\_ betanews](https://betanews.com/) [>\_ betanews](https://betanews.com/) * [Home](/) * [AI](/topic/ai/) * [Technology](/topic/technology/) * [Software](/topic/software/) * [Hardware](/topic/hardware/) * [Security](/topic/security/) * [About Us](/about/) [Windows 11](https://betanews.com/topic/windows-11/) [Microsoft](/topic/microsoft/) [Apple](/topic/apple/) [Linux](/topic/linux/) [Cloud](/topic/cloud/) [ChatGPT](https://betanews.com/topic/chatgpt/) [AI](https://betanews.com/topic/ai/) [Security](/topic/security/) Monday, November 9, 2026 [Contact us](https://betanews.com/contact/) [AI (Artificial Intelligence)](https://betanews.com/topic/ai/) # Hanselman’s gputaskman reveals which apps and AI models fill your VRAM ![Marcus Pruitt](https://media.betanews.com/uploads/2026/07/MarcusPruitt-96x96.png) By [Marcus Pruitt](https://betanews.com/author/marcus-pruitt/) Published [Preferred source](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=betanews.com "Add BetaNews as a preferred source in Google") Share Share Scott Hanselman has released [gputaskman](https://github.com/shanselman/gputaskman), a free terminal app that splits GPU memory use out by process and points to the AI models loaded on a local machine. Currently a VP and Member of Technical Staff with Microsoft and GitHub, he published the code as open source under the MIT license. His README pitches the project as “An htop for what’s inside your GPU, not just how full it is.” The documentation frames its purpose around a Task Manager reading of 15 GB used, asking how much of that goes to model weights, the KV cache or a web browser. Announcing it on X on November 3, Hanselman wrote that he was building the tool “to get insights to where my GPU memory is going,” and invited pull requests. A follow-up reply in the same thread linked straight to the repository. > There's a lot going on in my GPU. I'm making a GPU Taskman to get insights to where my GPU memory is going. PRs welcome https://t.co/6FwKqnFWDW > > — Scott Hanselman 🌮 (@shanselman) [November 3, 2026](https://x.com/shanselman/status/2117419804189741408?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw) [Windows Task Manager](https://betanews.com/topic/task-manager/) offers total GPU load, utilization and temperature on its Performance tab. Memory columns for individual processes can be enabled under Details, though the setting is tucked away and reveals little about each program’s activity. Owners of NVIDIA cards can pin the NVIDIA GPU Activity monitor on their taskbar, yet it only names whichever processes are touching the graphics chip at that moment. Anything deeper has typically required PowerShell commands. Inside gputaskman, a device view charts VRAM consumption, temperature, GPU and memory activity, power draw and PCIe traffic, meaning data passed between the graphics card and the PC. Clock speeds, encode and decode activity and history graphs fill out that screen, and machines with several GPUs get a separate header and chart set for each one. Every process using the GPU gets its own row in the process view, listing local VRAM, host memory reachable by the GPU tagged Spill, an estimate of non-resident commit tagged Paged, plus engine load across 3D, compute, copy and video work. Runtime detection covers CUDA, HIP, Vulkan, Direct3D, ggml and ONNX Runtime. For anyone running an [LLM](https://betanews.com/topic/llm/) locally, the Model inspector does the heaviest lifting. It sorts each loaded model by kind, then reports quantization, architecture, layer count, weight size and an estimated KV cache cost alongside the VRAM a process holds. Quantization is a compression method that lets a model occupy less memory. Detection works with llama.cpp, LM Studio, Ollama and stable-diffusion.cpp. Each identification comes with evidence, such as an API response, a mapped file or a command-line argument. Scripts can pull the same numbers through a --json snapshot or a record mode that logs readings...

Infra & Chips.content: * [Login](https://www.thelec.net/member/login.html) * [Join](https://www.thelec.net/member/index.html) * [Mobile](https://www.thelec.net/member/index.html) * UPDATE : 2026-11-10 08:53 (Tues) * [KOREAN](http://www.thelec.kr/) [![The Elec Inc.](https://cdn.thelec.net/image/logo/toplogo_20260408103815.png)](https://www.thelec.net) [![The Elec Inc.](https://cdn.thelec.net/image/logo/printlogo_20260408103815.png)](https://www.thelec.net) Rebellions, Nvidia to Build Sovereign AI Infrastructure in Korea Character Size Settings 가 The body content of the article will be changed to this letter size. 스크롤 이동 상태바 # Rebellions, Nvidia to Build Sovereign AI Infrastructure in Korea ## R200-based AI inference rack to be developed and tested at SK Telecom data centers * JEONG IL JOO * Published 2026.11.10 08:51 * Reply 0 Character Size Settings 가 가 The body content of the article will be changed to this letter size. 이 기사를 공유합니다 ![](https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/202611/15444_15767_659.jpg) Rebellions is partnering with Nvidia and SK Telecom (SKT) to build a Korean-standard sovereign artificial intelligence (AI) computing infrastructure based on next-generation neural processing units (NPUs). The project will connect Rebellions’ NPUs with Nvidia’s open infrastructure platform through NVLink Fusion, with the resulting systems to be deployed and tested at SKT’s AI data centers. Rebellions CEO Park Sung-hyun unveiled the plan at Nvidia AI Day Seoul 2026 on Nov. 9. The three companies signed a memorandum of understanding (MOU) the same day. Rebellions will develop a rack-scale AI inference system using its next-generation R200 NPU and Nvidia’s MGX server rack architecture. The R200 succeeds the R100 NPU, which is equipped with fifth-generation high-bandwidth memory (HBM3E). The system will use NVLink Fusion interconnect technology to enable a scale-up architecture connecting the NPU with AI computing platforms, including central processing units (CPUs) and graphics processing units (GPUs), within a server rack. The R200 is being designed for low-latency, high-efficiency inference of frontier AI models, including mixture-of-experts (MoE) models. Rebellions aims to begin supplying R200 systems in 2028. By leveraging Nvidia’s MGX ecosystem, the company plans to shorten rack system development timelines and reduce deployment risks. SKT will deploy the system in its AI data centers for testing under real-world operating conditions. The system will use a distributed inference approach that assigns different stages of AI inference to the most suitable chips, including GPUs and NPUs. This is expected to reduce power consumption and total cost of ownership (TCO) for large-scale AI services. The three companies aim to establish a “Sovereign AI Token Factory,” a sovereign AI data center infrastructure designed to generate tokens at scale. They plan to introduce standards applicable across public institutions and the private sector and accelerate market adoption. Rebellions intends to build a track record through deployments at SKT’s AI data centers and public-facing services before expanding its presence in overseas markets. ![JEONG IL JOO의 프로필 이미지](https://cdn.thelec.net/news/photo/member/1week_20250825010403.jpg) [JEONG IL JOO](https://www.thelec.net/news/articleList.html?sc_area=I&sc_word=1week&view_type=sm) [1week@thelec.kr](mailto:1week@thelec.kr) [View other news](https://www.thelec.net/news/articleList.html?sc_area=I&sc_word=1week&view_type=sm) Copyright © The Elec Inc. Infra & Chips.content: # Rebellions R200 NPU Racks Get NVLink Fusion, With NVIDIA GPUs on Prefill and NPUs on Decode, Deploying in 2028 NVIDIA, Rebellions, and SK Telecom announced a plan to build sovereign AI inference infrastructure in South Korea around Rebellions’ next-generation R200 neural processing unit, connected inside the rack with NVIDIA NVLink Fusion and built on the NVIDIA MGX rack architecture. SK Telecom will deploy the systems in its AI data center alongside its models and services. The three companies expect R200 systems to be ready for deployment in 2028. ## NVLink Fusion Connects R200 NPUs Rebellions is designing the R200 for low-latency, energy-efficient inference on frontier models, including multitrillion-parameter mixture-of-experts models. [NVLink Fusion](https://www.storagereview.com/news/the-network-is-the-accelerator-inside-the-technologies-powering-ai-factories) is NVIDIA’s program for bringing custom silicon onto its scale-up fabric: a chipmaker integrates NVLink into its processor and gains access to NVIDIA’s NVLink switching, its high-bandwidth, low-latency networking, and the surrounding infrastructure ecosystem. Rebellions plans to use it to link R200 NPUs within a rack over NVLink scale-up networking and to tie those processors into the NVIDIA platform as part of a rack-scale system. The companies have not disclosed R200 specifications, the NVLink bandwidth per NPU, or any performance results for the planned configuration. Rebellions lists the Rebel100 as its current silicon, and the R200 announcement says nothing about memory, process node, or power, so the step between the two generations is unknown. ## MGX Rack Architecture Supports System Development NVIDIA’s [MGX rack architecture](https://www.storagereview.com/news/msi-ocp-2026-liquid-cooled-cg681-s6093-mgx-rack-32-rtx-pro-6000) and reference designs give Rebellions a starting point for the system, along with access to the original design manufacturers and component suppliers already building MGX hardware. MGX defines the shared pieces of a rack, including footprint, power delivery, and cooling, so GPU systems and NPU systems can occupy the same data center design. SK Telecom plans to deploy the R200 systems in its AI data center on the standardized MGX rack, which lets it plan power and cooling before the processor is final. ## GPUs for Prefill, NPUs for Decode The most interesting technical detail is the inference split the three companies plan to develop. Inference has two phases with different hardware demands: prefill, which processes the prompt and is typically compute-bound, and decode, which generates tokens one at a time and is typically bound by memory bandwidth and latency. The proposed configuration runs prefill on NVIDIA GPUs and decode on Rebellions NPUs, with the two connected over the NVLink fabric. The stated goals are higher inference throughput and better power efficiency. The benefit of handing decode to an NPU remains a design intent until systems exist, but the logic makes sense on paper. Disaggregated prefill and decode is already common practice across GPU pools, including in NVIDIA’s Dynamo serving framework; splitting the two phases across different processor architectures over NVLink is the new part. Rebellions cofounder and CEO Sunghyun Park said the collaboration combines the company’s AI silicon and system design with NVIDIA’s interconnect and rack-scale capabilities and SK Telecom’s models and data center operations, with the aim of low-latency, energy-efficient inference for frontier models at scale. ## SK Telecom Connects Models and Services SK Telecom brings the models and the customers. It plans to run its proprietary foundation models, including A.X K2, on the infrastructure, along with public-facing services developed through the Korean government’s AI for All project. This Is the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Chip Stock Nvidia Should Fear Most. ![The Motley Fool](https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/logos/light/aol_the_motley_fool_392.png) ![An engineer designing a semiconductor chip.](https://hermes.media.transform.aol.com/ae85f5f299f46ab33647361f4c7ec934341b1670/w_1200,c_scale,f_auto,q_auto/https://hermes.media.static.aol.com/media/2026/11/09/9cd36edc-3669-3533-9b66-51b987553575/e437d521-4234-4e56-bf08-b37a371e5e40.jpg) ## Key Points Nvidia dominates the artificial intelligence (AI) data center industry thanks to its roster of GPUs. AMD and Intel design their own AI GPUs and CPUs that compete with Nvidia's chip architectures. AI hyperscalers are increasingly investing in custom silicon, a market currently dominated by Broadcom. [Motley Fool Issues Rare "Total Conviction" Buy Alert ›](https://api.fool.com/infotron/infotrack/click?apikey=35527423-a535-4519-a07f-20014582e03e&impression=73f72864-608a-41ad-be33-1cdece2ac60a&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.fool.com%2Fmms%2Fmark%2Fa-sa-dd-total-conviction%3Faid%3D11123%26source%3Disaedikp0000104%26ftm_cam%3Dsa-dd%26ftm_veh%3Dkeypoints_pitch_feed_msn%26ftm_pit%3D20178&utm_source=AolDailyFinance&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=566f8424-a0f7-4a34-827a-cf683546c070) **Nvidia** (NASDAQ: NVDA) has dominated the semiconductor market throughout the artificial intelligence (AI) revolutions. Its [graphics processing units](https://www.fool.com/terms/g/gpu/?utm_source=AolDailyFinance&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=article&referring_guid=566f8424-a0f7-4a34-827a-cf683546c070) (GPUs) are essential infrastructure for companies developing generative AI models. Naturally, investors are focusing on competitors like **Advanced Micro Devices** (NASDAQ: AMD) and **Intel** (NASDAQ: INTC), both of which make their own GPU and CPU architectures. However, I think Nvidia's biggest competitive threat could come from an entirely different direction. ***Missed Nvidia in 2009? With major customers including **Alphabet** (NASDAQ: GOOGL) (NASDAQ: GOOG), **Meta Platforms** (NASDAQ: META), OpenAI, and Anthropic, **Broadcom** (NASDAQ: AVGO) is emerging as a formidable competitor for future AI infrastructure spending. Here's why smart investors should pay attention. ## Broadcom is helping Nvidia's biggest customers make their own chips Nvidia's GPUs are useful because they can handle a wide variety of accelerated computing tasks. However, that flexibility isn't always necessary. Infra & Chips.content: [Skip to content](#main-content) [![](https://www.engineering.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Engineering.com_color-TM-scaled.png)](https://www.engineering.com) [Subscribe](https://www.engineering.com/subscribe/) [Industry News](https://www.engineering.com/category/industry/industry-news/) # NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom advance Korea’s sovereign AI The collaboration will integrate Korean-designed R200 processors with NVIDIA's NVLink Fusion and MGX rack architecture for AI deployment. NVIDIA, Rebellions and SK Telecom announced a collaboration to advance Korea’s sovereign AI infrastructure — using NVIDIA NVLink Fusion to bring together NVIDIA’s open infrastructure platform, Rebellions’ Korean-designed AI processors and SK Telecom’s AI data center, model and service capabilities. As part of the agreement, Rebellions will use NVLink Fusion to connect its Rebel R200 neural processing units (NPUs) to the NVIDIA platform, and harness the NVIDIA MGX rack architecture for rack-scale system development. SK Telecom plans to deploy these systems, drawing on its AI data center operations expertise, proprietary models and services. Supported by Korea’s Ministry of Science and ICT (MSIT), the collaboration aims to support AI services tailored to Korea’s language, industries and priorities, connecting Korean semiconductor development with the systems and operational capabilities needed to deliver AI at scale. ### **Scaling silicon innovation with NVIDIA’s open infrastructure platform** NVLink Fusion extends NVIDIA’s vertically integrated, horizontally open AI platform to custom XPUs. It enables chipmakers to combine specialized silicon with NVIDIA’s high-bandwidth, low-latency scale-up networking and established infrastructure ecosystem, helping improve performance, reduce deployment risk and accelerate time to market. Rebellions is developing its next-generation R200 NPU, optimized for low-latency and energy-efficient inference using frontier models, including multitrillion-parameter [mixture-of-experts](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/glossary/mixture-of-experts/) models. Through NVLink Fusion, Rebellions will connect its R200 NPUs within a rack through [NVIDIA NVLink](https://www.nvidia.com/en-us/data-center/nvlink/) scale-up networking. The NVIDIA MGX rack architecture and reference designs will support development of the systems, while the MGX ecosystem gives Rebellions access to an established supply chain of original design manufacturers and component suppliers. ### **Connecting infrastructure, models and services** SK Telecom brings experience building and operating AI data centers, alongside its proprietary foundation models and public-facing AI services. Building on its [long-standing collaboration with NVIDIA](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/sk-telecom-ai-infrastructure) in AI development and sovereign infrastructure, SK Telecom plans to connect these capabilities and deploy them in its AI data center using the standardized MGX rack architecture to deliver full-stack sovereign AI. The MGX rack architecture provides a foundation for GPU and NPU systems to share data center design elements, including rack footprint, power delivery and cooling. This approach can support infrastructure planning alongside Rebellions’ processor and system development. The companies plan to develop an approach to disaggregated inference, assigning different stages of AI response generation to the processor architecture best suited to each task. Their planned work includes using NVIDIA GPUs for prefill and Rebellions NPUs for decode to improve inference throughput and power efficiency. Infra & Chips.content: IT Brief Asia - Technology news for CIOs & IT decision-makers [![IT Brief Asia logo](/brands/itb-new-logo.svg)](/) [Powered By ![TechDay logo](/brands/td-new-logo-right.svg)](https://techday.asia) ![Dell expands AI factory with NVIDIA for agentic AI](https://itbrief.asia/uploads/story/2026/11/09/jensen-huang-and-michael-dell-story-323915.webp) [Edge Computing](https://itbrief.asia/tag/edge-computing) [DC](https://itbrief.asia/tag/data-centers) [AI](https://itbrief.asia/tag/artificial-intelligence) # Dell expands AI factory with NVIDIA for agentic AI Mon, 9th Nov 2026 (Today) [![Mara Sugue](https://itbrief.asia/rails/active_storage/representations/redirect/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6MTg1OSwicHVyIjoiYmxvYl9pZCJ9fQ==--c35d782a2ad379dbb3ebd1d7a0269b918cf68f7f/eyJfcmFpbHMiOnsiZGF0YSI6eyJmb3JtYXQiOiJ3ZWJwIiwicmVzaXplX3RvX2ZpbGwiOlsxNjAsMTYwXSwicXVhbGl0eSI6ODV9LCJwdXIiOiJ2YXJpYXRpb24ifX0=--89ddf5e6765c65a563c2258053e9d33c05d195da/maraheadshot.webp) MARA SUGUE News Editor](/author/mara-sugue) Dell has expanded its Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA with new software, deskside systems and data-centre infrastructure for agentic AI. More than 6,500 customers have adopted the offering. The update includes validated models and software, managed services, desktop and workstation configurations, modular data-centre designs and new PowerEdge servers for organisations running AI workloads on their own infrastructure. Dell is positioning the package around a growing enterprise push to move agentic AI projects beyond the pilot stage. It said businesses want greater control over data, operations and costs as they deploy AI agents more widely across development teams, office environments and core infrastructure. Among the software additions, Reflection's Beam open-weight model has been validated on the Dell AI Factory with NVIDIA. Dell also added or updated ecosystem programme solutions for AI observability with Dynatrace, a knowledge assistant and agentic AI platform with Mistral, and computer vision with Fogsphere. SUSE Linux will be added as an operating system option for the stack. Dell also outlined a layered security approach combining Dell infrastructure, the NVIDIA OpenShell Reference Architecture for runtime governance and Red Hat AI Factory software for orchestration. Dell said the templates set out the hardware, models and software stack for uses including agentic coding, agentic VSS, NVIDIA NemoClaw, Hermes Agent on NemoClaw and a higher education AI lab platform. According to Dell, the templates are designed to scale from a single developer system to deployments of 1,000 or more systems. It also introduced a 64GB unified memory configuration for Dell Pro Precision with GB10, aimed at individual developers and smaller teams working on local agentic AI development. The desktop can be linked in clusters of two or four systems to support larger models and more complex workflows. So it is with two new TPU accelerators that Google will be rolling out next year for its eponymous cloud and maybe even for some of its handful of direct customers who can get their hands on iron based on Google’s homegrown compute engines for their own datacenters. To be specific, there are two new variants of the “Sunfish” TPU 8t and “Zebrafish” TPU 8i accelerators that [Google first revealed back in April of this year](https://www.nextplatform.com/compute/2026/04/24/with-tpu-8-google-makes-genai-systems-much-better-not-just-bigger/5218834). The TPU 8t is made at the behest of Google by Broadcom’s chip shepherding unit and is expected to be rolling into Google datacenters right now. The TPU 8i is being shepherded by MediaTek and earlier this year had experienced some delays; it is unclear if it is shipping to Google now or not. The modified versions of these Sunfish and Zebrafish systems are expected to be installed sometime in 2027, and we are optimistically predicting that this will start happening in Q1 2027 with ramping happening over the next year and a half until the machines are available in multiple Google Cloud regions around the globe. These ramps take time. NEXTPLATFORM AD For instance, in the interim between the Sunfish and Zebrafish announcements in April and today, Google rolled out the predecessor “Ironwood” TPU v7p accelerators, which were first deployed in Q4 2025 for the company’s internal use, onto the Google Cloud and actually put pricing out for them in its US-Central1 region in Iowa and its Europe-West2 region outside London. My monster TPU table below has this updated pricing included. It took approximately a year for enough excess Ironwood capacity to be available that Google could put it out for rent on the cloud. Let’s drill down into the new Sunfish and Zebrafish systems. The TPU 8t was explicitly designed to run AI training workloads, and it supports Google’s 3D torus interconnect that spans 9,600 accelerators in a shared coherent memory space and that delivers a stunning 121 exaflops of oomph at FP4 precision. Each Sunfish 8i device has 216 GB of HBM3E memory across six stacks. This is by far the largest shared memory computing footprint in the AI space, and you can bet that Google wants as many TPU 8t accelerators as it can get out of Broadcom and chip foundry partner Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co so it can train up its Gemini frontier models. On a conference call going over the new TPU machines, Mark Lohmeyer, vice president and general manager of AI and computing infrastructure at Google, said that these machines are organized into the 9.600-unit pods and then ganged up to create a cluster with over 1 million TPU 8t devices, and that such a cluster was indeed used to train the Gemini 4 Carbon frontier model that was delayed a bit and giving the company a certain amount of heartburn. Gemini 4 Carbon, developed by its DeepMind unit, [was announced on October 28](https://blog.google/innovation-and-ai/models-and-research/gemini-models/introducing-gemini-4-carbon/).
